steps.text: Place raspberries in the bowl of a food processor; blend until smooth. If an extra smooth sorbet is desired, press pureed raspberries through a fine sieve to remove seeds. Whisk together pureed raspberries and honey in a large bowl.

Combine 3 cups of water, sugar, and corn syrup in a large saucepan; stir to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat. Boil until sugar is dissolved, without stirring, about 2 minutes. Stir sugar water and remaining 1 cup of water into raspberry puree.

Make an ice bath by filling a very large bowl with water and ice. Set the bowl of raspberry puree in the ice bath, and whisk until cool. Pour cooled puree into a 9x13-inch baking dish; cover and freeze until solid, 6 to 8 hours.
To make a coarsely textured granita, use a fork to scrape frozen puree into small crumbs. For a deliciously silky sorbet, transfer frozen puree to a food processor and process until smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Raspberry Sorbet
raw_recipe.description: This raspberry sorbet is a refreshing frozen treat full of fresh raspberry flavor for a delicious way to cool down on a hot summer's day!

review.reviewBody: You can substitute strawberries, but I found that it needed a cup less water, which made it sweeter. Use your discretion. But works just fine as the recipe states.. just makes more sorbet!

Excellent. Followed recipe; strained out the seeds. Half the batch was frozen in freezer. This creates more ice crystals although stirring it up brings it back to a slushy consistency. Other half refrigerated over night and made using an ice cream machine. In the future, prefer making this in an ice cream machine as the texture is noticeably smoother with the entire batch having the same consistency.

This recipe is very refreshing! I only made a few changes. I used frozen raspberries, the juice of 1 lime, used less honey and increased the sugar to 1 cup. I did use my ice cream maker - 45 minutes and it was perfect. My 6 year old did not like the seeds so I strained a batch for her and she was happy.

YUMMY! I made this recipe for tonight's dessert. I followed the recipe except for the freezing. Since I didn't have 6 hours for it to freeze, I froze it for an hour to get it cold, then put it into my ice cream machine. The end result was a yummy raspberry sorbet. Thank you Toasted Garlic for sharing your recipe.

Made the recipe for the most part as written, but tweaked it a bit to our own tastes. I added the best of 1 lemon and the juice of half that lemon. I increased the recipe a bit just because that is how many black raspberries we picked. I also added maple syrup instead of honey as I didn't have enough honey on hand. I also added a dash of salt for balance- less than 1/4 tsp. Everyone loved it.

Very tasty use of the bucketful of about-to-go-bad raspberries my sister gave me. I strained out the seeds for a seedless sorbet. It took a while, and I had to constantly mix the pulp around to try to get the liquid to fall through the strainer. The leftover seedy/pulpy solids seemed to be almost equal in volume to the strained liquid, so I adjusted the measurements of the other ingredients accordingly. I froze it in the 9x13 pan overnight, much longer than 6-8 hours, but I was still able to pry it out to process it until smooth. I only processed a third of it for now, leaving the remainder in the 9x13 in the freezer until we want some again later..
Have to freeze in 9x13 so it freezes evenly. Strawberries work well with one less cup water. Freeze in 9x13 for 6-8 hrs and then re-run through food processor. Freeze 2 more hours.
The reviews I read were quite accurate. I made this according to the recipe, but ended up with too much water by accident, so it got a bit runny on thawing out. I will be making this again.
Very good. Did transfer the frozen puree to food processor and process until smooth!
I loved the texture and it was exactly the right consistency also the taste was very rich and a little tart.
Well written, easy to make and can be the starting point for many other fruit treats. Thank you for this recipe!
Delicious - especially when combined with Vanilla ice cream!
Wonderful Recipe! I made it using fresh organic raspberry's from my garden.
This recipe is REALLY good! It is really nice with organic, freshly picked and washed rasberries. A sweet taste fore everyone! You will get extra, so beware!
Made this twice and love it! Great hit among the family! Used fresh raspberrys from my garden. Delicious!
